title: Whole Budding Fronds and Solitary Rootlets Duckweed
description: One newly authored enlarged attached duckweed budding group, one whole model and zero scenes. A broad entire-margined mother frond carries two unequal daughter fronds by short lateral attachment stipes; each frond has exactly one complete dangling unbranched rootlet with a small terminal cap. The fronds are the reduced leaf-and-stem bodies, not leaves on long petioles. Newly authored domed obovate surfaces and under-root attachment geometry are not old waterlily notched pads, rhizome or petioles, a scaled liverwort thallus, or moss leaves copied into a new arrangement. Four subdued opaque green and root tones, all finite edges. Generic Lemna-like external morphology only, not an identified species, measured live specimen, underground root system or a claim of stable standing on the root tip. Short stipes locate budding margins, but internal budding pouch cavities, fine nerves, cells, air spaces, flowers and fruits are omitted. No water or soil plane, environmental scene, natural scale relationship, buoyancy, growth, motion, rig or simulation. Whole attached group is one asset, not three independently counted fronds or root parts.
